entry.label: Anthro-complexity
entry.description: A body of theory and practice concerned with complexity in human systems, foregrounding meaning, intentionality, identity, narrative and the limits of treating people as interchangeable agents.
entry.canonical_definition: A body of theory and practice concerned with complexity in human systems, foregrounding meaning, intentionality, identity, narrative and the limits of treating people as interchangeable agents.

profile.title: Anthro-complexity
profile.canonical_definition: A body of theory and practice concerned with complexity in human systems, foregrounding meaning, intentionality, identity, narrative and the limits of treating people as interchangeable agents.
profile.summary: Anthro-complexity addresses complexity in human systems without treating people as simple agents analogous to insects, particles or interchangeable units. It foregrounds meaning, play, making, narrative, identity and intentionality.
profile.why_it_matters: Human beings can act on descriptions, change identity, contest purposes and alter the rules. These capacities affect what can be carried across from computational or biological complexity models.
key_distinctions: meaning and identity vs behaviour alone
natural science constraint vs direct social analogy
common_misreadings: human systems are exempt from material constraint
computational complexity is rejected rather than bounded
anthro-complexity is the only account of social complexity
open_checks: compare with complex responsive processes and social complexity traditions
clarify relation to cybernetics and systems dynamics
